title: Longarm - give your coding agents a long arm

lines: Your coding agent just kicked off a full build.
Then a test suite. Then three more agents.
And your laptop is melting.
Meet Longarm.
Give your coding agents a long arm.
Agents are great at starting work, and terrible at waiting for it.
Meanwhile, there's a thirty-two core box under your desk, an old laptop, and a cloud VM, all doing nothing.
Longarm turns every one of them into a single pool of workers.
Install it on every machine you have.
Sign in once, with a single code.
Now each machine is a worker, and your laptop can hand it anything.
Type longarm run, and your command.
The scheduler picks a machine with free memory and CPU to spare, gives the job a fresh worktree of your checkout, and streams the output back.
Your fans stay quiet.
And it's built for agents.
One command installs the Longarm skill into Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Codex and Gemini.
Now you just say: run the tests on a worker.
Fan out five sub-agents, each on its own worker, in its own worktree.
Steer a remote agent while it runs, or hand off a whole conversation, uncommitted code and all, to another machine.
Jobs run detached.
Close the lid. Switch networks. Restart the daemon.
The job keeps running, and you re-attach right where you left off.
Workers behind home routers, or carrier-grade NAT?
Longarm races three transports at once: plain TCP, Tailscale, and its own QUIC with hole punching, with a relay as the fallback.
Everything is mutual TLS, end to end. The hub only coordinates, and even relayed traffic stays encrypted.
Attach to a remote terminal, tmux style.
Forward a dev server to localhost.
Sync your checkout. Use SSH and VS Code Remote, with no keys to manage.
And watch the whole fleet from the tray, or from the hub's web panel.
Getting started takes about three minutes.
Open your hub. Download the installer, or paste one line.
Approve the code in your browser. That's it.
Longarm. Give your coding agents a long arm.
